task.title: Persist finite fixed-interval recurrence definitions
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/859 by durably storing immutable, validated finite recurrence definitions without granting scheduling or execution authority.
acceptance_criteria: Persist and reload exact recurrence identity, goal, anchor, positive interval, positive occurrence count, final instant, and revision.
Reject invalid, overflowing, duplicate, malformed, unsupported, and multi-event definition state with typed evidence.
Document that definition persistence does not persist occurrences, read a clock, choose catch-up policy, dispatch, retry, or execute work.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused recurrence-store test failed to compile because the recurrence persistence API and types did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added integration coverage for exact persistence and reopen, duplicate creation, invalid values, overflow, and corrupted histories.

attempts.diagnostic: Finite recurrence arithmetic was already validated, but no durable definition boundary preserved its authored identity and exact projection inputs.
attempts.patch: Added typed recurrence identifiers and counts, strict version-1 event encoding and replay, exact load and create operations, and ADR-0037.

attempts.summary: Held the merge gate through a false-green review cooldown.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit initially reported a review limit, so its green status did not constitute substantive exact-head review evidence.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled, resumed review after the cooldown and shared-budget check, and merged only after exact-head CI, genuine review, and resolved threads.

outcome.summary: Vela durably stores and strictly replays immutable finite fixed-interval recurrence definitions while leaving occurrence lifecycle and execution authority deferred.

lessons: Validate the representable final occurrence before making a recurrence definition durable.
One immutable event per definition keeps replay strict and leaves future mutation semantics explicit.
Persisting authored timing intent is not permission to decide due state or execute work.
A rate-limited green review status must not arm merge.
